thing-type.label: Scene
thing-type.description: Triggers an existing scene, programmed via the HDL Buspro Setup Tool, from openHAB. This is not a physical device - Subnet/DeviceID identify which device on the bus to send the trigger to (any device that is a member of the target area works), Area/Scene identify which scene to run.

channel.description: Sending ON triggers the configured scene. The state is not read back from the bus - this only sends a Scene_Control command, it does not track the scene's resulting channel values (see the DimChannel/RelayCh channels on the affected dimmer/relay Things for that).

parameter.name: Subnet
parameter.label: Subnet
parameter.description: Subnet of the device to send the scene trigger to.

parameter.name: DeviceID
parameter.label: Device ID
parameter.description: Device ID of the device to send the scene trigger to.

parameter.name: area
parameter.label: Area
parameter.description: The area number the scene is configured under (see the HDL Buspro Setup Tool).

parameter.name: scene
parameter.label: Scene
parameter.description: The scene number to trigger (see the HDL Buspro Setup Tool).

channel-type.label: Curtain Travel Duration
channel-type.description: Full-travel duration for this curtain channel, as configured on the device itself and queried automatically at startup - use this value as the "uptime"/"downtime" parameter for the ROLLERSHUTTERPOSITION profile on the matching Shutter*Control channel's Item link (see the README's "Curtain Position (MW02)" section). Unit assumed seconds, not formally confirmed. Stays undefined if the device doesn't respond to the query.

channel-type.label: Floor Heating Temperature Unit
channel-type.description: Temperature unit (C or F) the DLP panel is reporting floor heating setpoints in.

channel-type.label: Floor Heating Timer Period
channel-type.description: Which schedule period (Day or Night) is currently active; only meaningful when FHMode is Timer.

channel-type.label: Music Command
channel-type.description: Raw command the panel's "Music" tab sends its onboard Z-Audio engine when a Play/Stop/ source button is pressed (e.g. "ON", "SRC+") - confirmed via real hardware capture that this panel family talks a plain-text "*Z<zone><command>" protocol here regardless of what's configured in the HDL Setup Tool's Music CMD list. Updates on every button press, including repeats of the same command, so rules should use an "received update" trigger rather than "changed" if you need every press to fire. The vocabulary beyond "ON"/"SRC+" is not fully mapped yet - treat unfamiliar values as new data points, not something already understood.

channel-type.label: UV Switch
channel-type.description: Universal Switch - a generic HDL Buspro on/off flag; what it's assigned to is decided in the HDL Setup Tool project, not by this binding. Add one of these per switch number you actually need (see the "switchNumber" parameter below) - this thing type does not declare a fixed list of channels.

parameter.name: switchNumber
parameter.label: Switch Number
parameter.description: Which HDL universal switch number this channel represents (see the HDL Setup Tool). HDL's documented range is 1-248; on a Logic module (ML01) specifically, only 201-248 are valid (each Logic module gets 2 reserved numbers in that range) - numbers below 201 won't mean anything there.
